wizard.exclusive: Choosing this clears your other choices.
wizard.intro: A few quick questions, so BizCost shows only what your business uses.

name.title: What's your business called?
name.hint: The name your customers know, like your shop or Instagram name, or your own name. You can change it later.

sell_products.label: I sell products I buy ready-made

make_products.label: I make products (not food)
make_products.hint: Furniture, metal work, 3D printing, handmade items, factory goods

food_drinks.label: I make food or drinks
food_drinks.hint: Café, restaurant, bakery, cakes and sweets, home kitchen

projects.label: I do projects for clients
projects.hint: Big jobs in stages, with workers and materials: fit-out, contracting, events

catalog.label: The same items again and again
catalog.hint: A set list of products or designs

custom_jobs.label: Made to order for each customer
custom_jobs.hint: To the customer's size, drawing or file, e.g. furniture, steel gates, signs

shop.label: A shop, café, restaurant or showroom

kitchen.label: A commercial kitchen
kitchen.hint: A central or cloud kitchen, not at home

branches.title: Does your business have more than one branch?
branches.hint: Count your own shops, offices, workshops or stores, not your customers' places.

alone.label: No, just me
alone.hint: Even if family helps now and then without pay, or a freelancer does a job for me

team.label: Yes, one person or more
team.hint: Employees, workers, partners or paid family members

team_tracking.title: What do you want to track for your team?

hours.label: Working hours and overtime
hours.hint: Also used to count labour in your costs

salaries.label: Paying salaries, with advances and deductions

staff_cash.label: Cash given to staff for purchases

cost_only.label: Just what my team costs, for now

work_setup.title: Which of these apply to your work?
work_setup.hint_included: The materials you buy to make or sell are already covered, so they aren't listed here. Choose all that apply.

materials.label: I use materials or supplies
materials.hint: Paint, parts, salon products, building materials

stock.label: I keep stock and count what's left
stock.hint: Raw materials or goods on shelves that get restocked. Skip it if you buy what you need for each order.

machines.label: I want to count machine time in my costs
machines.hint: 3D printers, CNC, laser cutters, saws, welding, production lines

vehicles.label: I have vehicles for the business
vehicles.hint: Cars, vans, motorbikes or a staff bus used mainly for work. Not a personal car.

sales_channels.title: How do customers order and pay?

walk_in.label: They buy in person at my shop

messages.label: They order by WhatsApp, Instagram or phone
messages.hint: Then I deliver or they pick it up

online.label: Through my website, marketplaces or delivery apps
online.hint: Like Amazon, Noon, Talabat or Deliveroo

quotes.label: I send a written quote before I start
quotes.hint: For bigger jobs, custom work or events

invoice_later.label: I invoice them and they pay later
invoice_later.hint: Companies, purchase orders (LPO), wholesale or monthly accounts

pos.title: Do you have a cashier system (POS)?
pos.hint: If you have one, keep using it. You'll be able to import its daily sales from a file.

vat.title: Is your business registered for VAT?
vat.hint: Choose Yes only if it has a tax registration number (TRN). You can change this later.

yes.label: Yes, registered
yes.hint: It has a tax registration number (TRN)

review.title: Here's your BizCost
review.subtitle: Built from your answers. Turn off anything you don't need.
review.banner: BizCost opens in stages. The sections below are saved with your setup, and each one will appear by itself when it's ready.
review.teamNote: Your team sees only what you allow. Costs and profit stay hidden from them unless you give access.
review.vatNotSure: You chose Not sure, so VAT options are off for now. Turn them on once you have a TRN.
review.needsVat: Needs VAT registration. Turn on VAT under About your business first.
review.rateLimited: You have set up the most businesses allowed for today. Try again tomorrow.
review.alreadyCreated: {{businessName}} was already created from this setup with your earlier answers. What you changed after that was not saved.
review.createAnother: Create a new business with these answers

ready.title: Your BizCost is ready
ready.body: {{businessName}} is set up. Each section will appear here as soon as it's ready.

keeps_stock.on: You keep stock and count it

uses_machines.on: Machine time counts in your costs

sells_via_pos.on: Your sales come from your POS

jobs_and_tasks.on: Cost and profit for each job
jobs_and_tasks.on_maker: Cost and profit for each order

jobs.name: Cost and profit of each job
jobs.name_maker: Cost and profit of each order
jobs.desc: See what each job costs you and what you earn from it.
jobs.desc_maker: See what each order costs you and what you earn from it.

reason.custom_jobs: Each job is made to the customer's request, so see what each one costs you and what you earn.
reason.custom_jobs_maker: Each order is made to the customer's request, so see what each order costs you and what you earn.
reason.services: Each job is different, so see what each one costs you and what you earn.
reason.services_maker: Each order is different, so see what each one costs you and what you earn.

products.projects: List the services and work items you put in your quotes, and what each really costs.
products.services: List the services you offer and what each one really costs.
products.custom: Save what you price often, with its usual unit, to price new orders faster.
products.default: List what you sell and see what each one really costs.

materials.food: Track your ingredients and packaging, and what they cost.
materials.make: Track the materials that go into your products, and what they cost.
materials.resell: The goods you sell cost what you pay to buy them.
materials.uses: Count the materials and supplies you use in your costs.

suppliers.no_purchases: Save who you pay once, like software, printing or freelancers, and reuse them in expenses.
suppliers.projects: Save each supplier and subcontractor once, and reuse them in purchases and expenses.
suppliers.default: Save the shops and suppliers you buy from once, and reuse them.

purchases.default: What you pay when you buy sets your real costs.

expenses.default: Record every amount spent on the business, with or without a receipt.

running_costs.home: Count what working from home costs, like electricity, gas, internet and subscriptions.
running_costs.default: Count what you pay regularly to run your business, like rent, electricity and your licence.

files.default: Keep receipts and documents with your records.

cost_engine.jobs: See the true cost and profit of each job.
cost_engine.jobs_maker: See the true cost and profit of each order.
cost_engine.solo: See the true cost of your work, including your own time.
cost_engine.default: See the true cost of everything you sell or do.

customers.default: Save each customer once and use them everywhere.

sales.pos_apps: Import sales from your POS and delivery apps, with their fees, to see your real profit.
sales.pos: Import your POS sales to see your real profit.
sales.apps: Bring in sales from your online store or delivery apps, with their fees.
sales.with_orders: Add the sales you don't record as orders.
sales.invoices: Add any sales that don't come from your invoices.
sales.default: Add your sales to see your real profit.

payments.projects: Track deposits, stage payments and what each client still owes.
payments.deposits: Track deposits and what each customer still owes.
payments.orders: Know who paid, who paid a deposit and who still owes.
payments.default: Know who has paid and who still owes.

reports.projects: See your real profit by project, month and more.
reports.default: See your real profit by product, month and more.

orders.invoice_later: Follow each order until it's delivered and paid.
orders.custom_jobs: Keep each customer's order in one place, from deposit to delivery.
orders.messages: Keep WhatsApp, Instagram and phone orders in one place, with delivery and payment.
orders.shop_no_pos: There's no POS in your shop, so record each sale here. If adding daily totals is easier, turn this off.

quotations.projects: Give each project a written price before you start.
quotations.quotes: Prepare written quotes for your customers before you start.

invoices.projects: Send invoices, including stage invoices for each project.
invoices.vat: Your business is registered for VAT, so send tax invoices to your customers.
invoices.quotes: Turn accepted quotes into invoices and get paid.
invoices.default: Send invoices to your customers and follow what they owe.

inventory.default: See how much is left in stock.

usage_waste.make: See how much material goes to offcuts, failed pieces and waste, and what it costs.
usage_waste.resell: See what you lose to expired or damaged goods, and gaps you can't explain.
usage_waste.default: Compare expected usage from your sales with actual usage, and see where the difference goes.

employees.default: Others work with you, so their cost is part of your true cost.

equipment.default: Count what each machine costs per hour, including power and upkeep.

vehicles.default: See what your vehicles cost, like fuel and upkeep.

projects.default: See each project's costs (materials, labour, extra work) and its profit.

petty_cash.default: Track cash given to staff until it's settled with receipts or returned.

vat_center.default: Prepare and check your VAT return, kept apart from your profit.

orders.outside_pos: Turn this on if some orders don't go through your POS.

invoices.pos_off: Your POS prints your receipts. Turn this on if you also need to send tax invoices, for example to companies.
